    Interactive & inline delighters

    interactive-delighters.Rmd

    delightkitr spreads across three surfaces — interactive HTML/JS/CSS widgets, static SVG appliqués for print, and TikZ for LaTeX. This article covers the two that live on the web: the interactive specimen (Surface 1) and the inline SVG ornaments (the ornament_html() bridge).

    The interactive specimen

    The reference delighter — the organic “mitosis” specimen the package is named after — is a self-contained canvas animation shipped in inst/js/. Because it carries its own <style> and <script>, it can’t live in a README (pandoc strips the script on build). An article can host it, and an iframe keeps its styles and script sealed off from the page:

    # Load the self-contained specimen shipped with the package
spec <- paste(
  readLines(
    system.file("js", "specimen.html", package = "delightkitr"),
    warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"
  ),
  collapse = "\n"
)

# The file is a template: give its {{ID}} placeholder a unique value
spec <- gsub("{{ID}}", "dk-specimen-1", spec, fixed = TRUE)

# Embed in an isolated iframe so its <script>/<style> can't collide with the page
tags$iframe(
  srcdoc  = spec,
  title   = "delightkitr interactive specimen",
  loading = "lazy",
  style   = "width:100%; height:520px; border:0; display:block;"
)

    That same pattern works in any Quarto HTML doc, R Markdown page, or Shiny app — read the file, substitute an id, drop it in an iframe.

    Inline SVG ornaments

    The static ornaments need no script at all. ornament_html() renders a grob to an inline <svg> string, so these embed anywhere and survive every rebuild. In a chunk, set results = "asis" and cat() the markup:

    cat(ornament_html(sunburst_grob(), width = 1.2, height = 1.2))
    cat(ornament_html(rosette_grob(), width = 1.2, height = 1.2))
    # A wide, short grob reads as a horizontal rule rather than a medallion
cat(ornament_html(rinceau_grob(), width = 4, height = 0.6))

    These are the same strings gt_ornament() drops into a gt table — the bridge is written once and reused across every HTML surface.

    Inline ornaments need the svglite package (it’s in Suggests). Install it if a chunk above errors on a missing device.
